title: Arithmetic lifts and semilinear paths of finite fibre functors
statement:
Let $K$ be a perfect field (every algebraic extension of $K$ is separable), let $L$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $K$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $Y=Y_0\times_K L$ [def-pc-base-change], assume $Y$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and choose a geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Write $\bar y_0$ for its composite with $Y\to Y_0$ and $i:L\hookrightarrow\Omega$ for its map of constants. Use the finite etale categories of [def-galois-categories], and let $F=F_{\bar y}$ and $F_0=F_{\bar y_0}$ be their fibre functors [def-galois-fibre-functor]. The structure maps induce homomorphisms as in [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], and give an exact sequence of profinite groups
$$
1\longrightarrow P:=\operatorname{Aut}(F)\xrightarrow{j}G:=\operatorname{Aut}(F_0)\xrightarrow{r}\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\longrightarrow1.
$$
Give $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ its inverse-limit topology over the finite Galois subextensions of $L/K$. Here $r$ is characterized on the finite constant covers $Y_0\times_K\operatorname{Spec}E$, for finite subextensions $K\subseteq E\subseteq L$, by the action $\tau\mapsto r(g)\circ\tau$ on $\operatorname{Hom}_K(E,L)$, identified with their geometric fibres using $i$. Identify $P$ with its image under $j$.

For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ put $h_\sigma=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma):Y\to Y$. The set $r^{-1}(\sigma)$ is canonically in bijection with the natural isomorphisms
$$
\lambda_s:F_{h_\sigma\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar y}.
$$
The bijection is specified by the following evaluation rule, which fixes its inverse convention. For any finite intermediate extension $E/K$ and finite etale cover $Q_E\to Y_E=Y_0\times_KE$, let $Q=Q_E\times_E L$ and let
$$
\iota_\sigma:F_{h_\sigma\bar y}(Q)\hookrightarrow F_0(Q_E),\qquad
\iota_1:F_{\bar y}(Q)\hookrightarrow F_0(Q_E)
$$
be the injections obtained by forgetting the $L$-structure. The image of $\iota_\sigma$ is the fibre of $Q_E\to Y_0$ whose map of constants $E\to\Omega$ is $i\circ\sigma|_E$, and the image of $\iota_1$ has map of constants $i|_E$. Regard $Q_E\to Y_0$ as a finite etale cover. For every $z\in F_{h_\sigma\bar y}(Q)$,
$$
 \iota_1(\lambda_{s,Q}(z))=s^{-1}\cdot\iota_\sigma(z).
$$
This rule is independent of the chosen finite model, and applies to all finite etale $Y$-covers and their morphisms. Via the canonical first-projection identification $F_{\bar y}(h_\sigma^*Q)\cong F_{h_\sigma\bar y}(Q)$ for base change [def-pc-base-change], the resulting bijections satisfy
$$
 \lambda_{s,Q}(g\cdot z)=(s^{-1}gs)\cdot\lambda_{s,Q}(z)\qquad(g\in P).
$$
On the left, $P$ acts on $F_{\bar y}(h_\sigma^*Q)$ by evaluation of the fibre functor; on the right it acts on $F_{\bar y}(Q)$. For $a\in P$,
$$
 \lambda_{as,Q}=\lambda_{s,Q}\circ a^{-1}_{h_\sigma^*Q}.
$$
Under the equivalence with finite locally constant sheaves of sets [thm-galois-lc-etale], these are the same natural isomorphisms of stalk functors and the same identities. No coefficient module, descent isomorphism or Weil group is part of this statement.

source.place: Tag 0BTX, lemma-ses-field (exact sequence and descent to finite separable subextensions); Tag 0BTV, lemma-limit (objects, morphisms and eventual equalities in finite etale covers); Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (fibre-functor actions), and Tag 0BNE, lemma-fundamental-group-Galois-group (Galois action on embeddings). The displayed semilinear-path correspondence and normalization are an agent formulation of those finite-fibre constructions, matching the pointed-universal-cover action of Weil II (1.1.12), p.152.

proof.text: Use the source arithmetic exact-sequence lemma for the quotient r, its Krull continuity, surjectivity, constant-cover action and geometric kernel. Define j by restriction along the first-projection fibre comparison. Its evaluation coordinates are conjugates of evaluation on pulled-back covers, hence it is continuous.

The finite-model fibre injection is postcomposition with its first projection. Naturality identifies its geometric automorphism action with j. Every geometric cover has a finite model by object descent, so equality after j implies equality on each such injection and then on every cover; thus j is injective. The fibre-product universal property also proves both scalar-labelled range identities.

For a natural path lambda from the moved geometric fibre functor to the original, restrict along p:X→X₀, identifying endpoints over X₀, and call the resulting automorphism q(lambda). Naturality of lambda inverse on the global sections of pulled-back constant covers gives r(q(lambda) inverse)=sigma. Indeed the section labelled tau has point labels i∘tau and i∘sigma∘tau at the original and moved endpoints. Taking finite simple subextensions K(a) and using injectivity of i identifies the two Galois automorphisms on each a.

The source theorem CategoryTheory.PreGaloisCategory.nonempty_iso_of_fiberFunctor supplies a path on the connected finite-etale Galois category. Pullback coherence gives q(lambda followed by a)=j(a)q(lambda) and q(B(a) followed by lambda)=q(lambda)j(a). The first identity and injectivity of j make q injective. For any t over sigma and any starting path lambda, t inverse times q(lambda) inverse is in ker r, hence equals j(a). Then lambda followed by a maps to t inverse. Thus lambda↦q(lambda) inverse is bijective; define Phi by its inverse. This uses the proved generic source-library isomorphism theorem directly, avoiding a reconstruction of paths by descent of all morphisms.

There is a canonical morphism from any base-changed finite model to the pullback of its arithmetic cover: use its first projection and its structure map. Naturality of lambda along this morphism identifies arithmeticModelFiber(lambda(z)) with q(lambda) applied to arithmeticMovedModelFiber(z). The inverse-bijection identity q(Phi(t))=t inverse proves the required normalization for all models at once.

Set c=Phi(t) inverse followed by B(a) followed by Phi(t). Then B(a) followed by Phi(t)=Phi(t) followed by c. Apply q and its two composition identities, using q(Phi(t))=t inverse, to obtain j(c)=t inverse j(a)t. Evaluating the path equation gives the requested conjugation identity. Applying injectivity of q to (j(a)t) inverse=t inverse j(a) inverse gives the lift-change formula.

Whiskering along the supplied finite-etale/FLC equivalence and along the fully faithful forgetful/ULift functor gives bijections of natural isomorphisms. Conjugate by the canonical point/Yoneda stalk comparisons. Their composition and inverse identities transfer the finite-path comparison, conjugation and lift-change equations to stalks. The Lean proof constructs these equivalences and proves both identities using full faithfulness.

split_report.summary: Prove the arithmetic exact sequence through finite constant covers, their stabilizers and the field-limit fundamental-group lemma, rather than making the exact-sequence clause a new node. Construct the specified s-inverse path on labelled fibres, prove model independence for all morphisms, and calculate both conjugation and lift change. Prove bijectivity by the natural-automorphism torsor argument and transfer to finite locally constant sets. One new statement-only limit lemma; no statement change, Lean writing or compilation.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NC-7dfa97c6e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's statement (unchanged and not weakened) and all 12 steps against the statement of every cited node and against Stacks pione.tex 0BTX (l.3469), 0BTV (l.3428), 0BN3, 0BND, 0BNE and 0BQ9. The tags and labels match. I recomputed the conventions myself. In step 2, the permutation is left multiplication u_N(1)τ, which gives r(g)∘τ, and it is a homomorphism. In step 6, s^{-1} moves the label iσ|_E to i|_E. Step 9 gives s^{-1}gs. Step 10 gives λ_{as}=λ_s∘a^{-1}. Step 11: s=tb^{-1} recovers any path λ, and λ_{as}=λ_s forces a=1 because h_σ^* is an equivalence. Every hypothesis holds where it is used: Y_E and Y_0 are connected by step 1; L/K is separable, algebraic and normal because K is perfect; Y_0 is separated of finite type for both limit nodes. The new node lem-wf-pi1-algebraic-field-limit is the second assertion of 0BTV, specialised to the constant-field system. Its extra assumption that X_L is connected is harmless and holds where step 4 uses it. I tested it on L=K and on finite L/K. It has no proof, its searches are recorded, its blueprint fields are correct, it does not restate a clause of the item, and rg over the DAG finds no duplicate of it or of the 0BTX exact sequence. The item is not a duplicate of the finite-field transport and twisted-path nodes either. Accepted tool uses: the six declared ones, and the undeclared generic off-unit Galois-category nodes lem-galois-pi1-functoriality, lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object and lem-fet-galois-category. Batch-5 check: the new citation lem-wf-finite-etale-field-limit-descent reaches lem-trf-finite-morphism-finite-presentation, which only says that a finite, locally finitely presented morphism is finitely presented (Stacks 01TR/01TQ). That is a general scheme fact; neither the trace-formula nor the Poincaré-duality assumption gives it, and it is not a step specific to their proofs, so I judge it outside the assumed statements. No SGA is cited. No fixes.
